summary: A 1950 L-4 cab on a stone base, the third lookout on this Clearwater National Forest point since 1916, now a recreation.gov rental reached via the historic Lolo Motorway.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 10-foot stone base, 14x14 ft with catwalk

access.note: Reached via the Lolo Motorway, a primitive CCC-built road not recommended for RVs, trailers or low-clearance vehicles; about a 100 ft walk up steep terrain from parking to the cabin.

visit.trail_note: About 100 feet of steep, rocky walking from the road to the lookout

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Clearwater National Forest, Lochsa Ranger District)

events.note: Frame cabin replaced by an R-1 log cabin with cupola
Current 14x14 ft L-4 cab with catwalk on a 10-foot stone base
Registered March 22, 2004 as US 573 / ID 43, nominated by Virginia Tillotson
Currently rehabbed and listed in the Forest Service recreation rental program

evidence.supports: 1916 frame cabin, 1928 log cabin replacement, 1950 current L-4 on stone base
evidence.quote: Castle Butte Lookout went into service on the Clearwater National Forest as a frame cabin in 1916. In 1928 it was replaced with an R-1 log cabin with cupola. The present 14'x14' L-4 cab with catwalk on a 10' stone base was built in 1950.
Recently rehabbed, it is now in the recreation rental system.

L-4 cab atop a 10' base, built in 1950, is presently on the Recreation Rental program.

evidence.supports: access via Lolo Motorway, built by CCC in early 1930s, follows Nez Perce/Lewis and Clark route, not recommended for RVs/trailers/low clearance
evidence.quote: Access to the lookout is via the Lolo Motorway, a primitive, single-lane road constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the early 1930s. It is not recommended for large RVs, vehicles with low ground clearance or trailers.
Guests should be prepared to walk about 100 feet up steep, rocky terrain to reach the lookout.

evidence.supports: sleeps four, amenities, no electricity or water
evidence.quote: Castle Butte Lookout can accommodate four people and comes equipped with two twin beds with foam mattresses, two cots, a table with two chairs, mop & bucket, a propane cook stove, propane lights, propane heater and propane. A pit toilet is located in a separate building outside.
The cabin does not have electricity or water.

evidence.supports: views of Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness, Seven Devils, Great Burn, North Fork Clearwater canyons
evidence.quote: It offers breathtaking, 360-degree views of the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness, the Seven Devils Mountains, the Great Burn area and the deep canyons of the North Fork Clearwater River's upper drainages.

evidence.supports: Lolo Trail historic route of Nez Perce and Lewis and Clark
evidence.quote: Hikers can follow the paths of the Nez Perce and Lewis and Clark on the historic Lolo Trail.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's conflict list shows 1950 (nhlr, ridb) vs 1928 (firelookout_com), but firelookout_com's own page text in fact gives the same three dates as nhlr: a 1916 frame cabin, a 1928 log cabin replacement, and the current 1950 L-4 cab. The apparent 1928 value in the tower record looks like a mis-extraction; all read sources agree 1950 is the build year of the structure standing today.

notes_for_editor: The tower record's 'conflicts' entry lists firelookout_com as giving a built year of 1928, but that page's actual text matches nhlr exactly (1916/1928/1950 sequence) — likely a mis-extraction when the record was built. Recommend the conflict be cleared rather than left open; no new correction filed since the record's 'built: 1950' field is already right. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed a sentence claiming secondary listings 'collapse' the three build dates and citing recreation.gov for the full 1916/1928/1950 sequence — no evidence quote supported that framing (recreation.gov's page does independently state the same three dates, confirmed by spot-check, but the sentence as written made an unsupported claim about other listings). Also rewrote the 1950-cab sentence, which copied the nhlr.org description almost verbatim.
